answer: One concrete Sybil defense is stake-backed identity: an agent must lock real value before it can forge a fresh account and cast a vote. To flood the network with thousands of fake names, an attacker has to split a glacier of capital across every single identity, and any node caught double-voting forfeits its whole deposit. Because detection slashes the bond, each fake name costs a stake as hard as quartz that is burned on fraud. Honest agents earn their lock back through fees, so the tax falls on quantity, not on telling the truth.
